CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right ankle injury

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old male who sustained a right ankle injury today while playing basketball with his son. Patient went up for a shot when his son collided with him, causing him to land awkwardly and twist his ankle. He reports pain on the lateral aspect of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. He has difficulty walking and reports the ankle feels unstable. Patient recently returned to a consistent workout routine at the gym and is concerned about disrupting this progress. Patient has also volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Meloxicam (prescribed)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Son Sean, age 10, plays basketball.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works from home. Has dogs. Recently returned to consistent exercise routine at the gym. Plays recreational basketball with son. Volunteered to coach basketball starting in April.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle: Swelling on the lateral side. Exquisite tenderness to palpation laterally. Some tenderness over the medial deltoid region. No epidermolysis. Skin intact. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment. Able to stand on ankle but has difficulty walking and reports instability.

RESULTS
Right ankle radiograph (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at the Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture, right ankle, at the Weber C level with unstable positioning. Surgical intervention recommended with placement of plate and screws. Patient prescribed meloxicam for pain and swelling management. Ice therapy and ankle elevation recommended. Crutches provided for ambulation support. Patient expected to be out of regular activities for approximately 3 months. Patient cleared to continue coaching as scheduled starting in April. Gradual return to exercise activities expected within the 3-month recovery period.
